extracted.intended_audience: Employees and representatives of Springer Nature (including managers, directors, suppliers, authors, editors and other business partners)
extracted.subtask_description: Company code of conduct setting behavioural, legal and ethical standards for Springer Nature employees and representatives, covering workplace conduct, conflicts of interest, data protection, anti‑corruption, supplier expectations and escalation routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct towards colleagues and others
rubrics_metrics.description: Working at Springer Nature means respecting the individual, embracing diversity, equality of opportunity, prohibiting discrimination and maintaining healthy and safe working conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees must treat colleagues fairly and respectfully; discrimination based on age, race, colour, nationality, descent, gender, religion, creed, sexual orientation or other personal characteristics is prohibited. Maintain workplaces free of harassment, unwanted physical contact, intimidation or bias. Avoid unsafe or illegal behaviour (including sale/use/possession of illegal drugs); exercise appropriate behaviour when legal drugs (e.g., alcohol) are present at business events. Employees may form in-house groups to represent interests. Commitment aligns with UN Universal Declaration of Human Rights, ILO guidelines, UN Convention on Children’s Rights and elimination of discrimination against women.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer Nature aims not only to comply with social, governance and environmental laws but often to exceed them, following frameworks such as the UN Global Compact and OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees should reduce environmental impact (e.g., continue print-to-digital conversion, use resources wisely, find sustainable alternatives). Be aware of and comply with international sanctions/restrictions (OFAC, UN, EU) when conducting business across territories and consult Compliance on questions. Contact the ESG Group for further information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection and proper use of Springer Nature’s assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Company funds, assets, facilities and equipment must be used only for legitimate business purposes and never for inappropriate, improper, unethical or illegal activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business trips should be appropriate and proportionate. Protect company assets from loss, damage or theft. Respect Springer Nature IP and third-party IP; obtain appropriate licences and permissions for software and content and consult Legal for licence questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest — disclosure and avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees must disclose any personal interests (including those of close or related parties) so the Company can decide if the interest creates a conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situations to disclose include: potential personal gain from a transaction; a colleague/candidate/supplier who is a close or related party; freelancing, consulting or part-time work for non-Springer Nature organisations; directly holding shares or voting rights in organisations that compete with or are customers/suppliers of Springer Nature. ‘Close or related parties’ include spouse, partner, co-habitee, child, parent/parent-in-law or sibling/sibling-in-law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of the media and separation of editorial/paid content
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer Nature will not enter into agreements that jeopardise editorial independence and maintains a clear separation of editorial and paid content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If advertisements or ‘Advertorial’ content appear in journals, make clear that it is not part of editorial content. Adhere to applicable press codes of practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and confidentiality (handling personal and confidential information)
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer Nature handles personal data and confidential business information responsibly and in compliance with applicable privacy/data protection laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and use personal data only for legitimate business purposes, limit access to those with a legitimate need, and take steps to prevent unauthorised access. Sensitive personal information requires additional protection and must not be disclosed except with proper authorisation or as required by law. Do not disclose non-public company information (operations, plans, financials) without valid business purpose and authorisation; use NDAs when sharing confidential information externally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online public forums and social media usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees identifiable as Springer Nature staff must exercise care on social media and online public forums; only authorised employees may post as company representatives or use company intellectual property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider type of information, audience, who can access it and system security. Only those specifically authorised may post on behalf of Springer Nature or use logos/trademarks/copyrighted material as company representation. Be aware employees may be seen as company representatives even if posting personally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair competition and antitrust compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer Nature competes fiercely but fairly and expects employees to deal fairly with customers, suppliers and competitors in compliance with competition/antitrust laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make business decisions in the best interests of the Company independent of any understanding with competitors. Consult the Legal Department before entering into any business discussion, agreement or relationship with a competitor (formal or informal). Violations carry severe criminal and civil penalties and can impact employees personally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corruption, fraud and bribery — zero tolerance
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer Nature prohibits any form of corruption, bribery or improper payments by anyone representing the Company, including within the supply chain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not offer, give or receive bribes or other benefits for personal or business gain. Zero tolerance globally — any payment or benefit that could be construed as securing unfair preferential treatment is prohibited. Do not offer facilitation/grease payments or gifts to government officials; avoid non-contractual payments, token appreciations, meals, entertainment or gifts that could be construed as attempts to obtain preferential treatment. Cash gifts or cash-equivalent gifts are never acceptable. When in doubt, decline and consult Compliance/Legal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record keeping and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Transactions must be recorded accurately and in a timely manner, with supporting documents reflecting underlying transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with local legal and tax requirements and retain records per legal notices (e.g., litigation holds). Dispose of records securely when no longer needed, preferably by secure shredding and recycling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply chain management and third-party due diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Third parties working with Springer Nature must meet the same ethical, health, safety and environmental standards set by the Company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer third parties with good reputations who support Springer Nature’s values and are transparent. Require engagement in due diligence and responsibility for their onward supply chain. Evaluate major suppliers on background, experience, reputation, cost, services, and commitment to business integrity and sustainability. Monitor major suppliers, agents and intermediaries throughout engagements to ensure ongoing compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working with governments and NGOs
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagements with public officials, governments or NGOs carry additional legal and ethical risks; public-sector interactions must strictly observe applicable laws and be centrally managed when political lobbying is involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public officials include foreign/domestic government officials, party officials or political candidates, employees of state-owned enterprises, employees of federal/local agencies, and employees of NGOs (e.g., World Bank, UN, WHO). Activities appropriate with commercial entities (gifts, hospitality) may be inappropriate or illegal with public officials; if engaging intermediaries on government/NGO business, ensure they understand additional risks. Political lobbying must be centralised and transparent; Springer Nature does not make political contributions (cash or in-kind, e.g., free printing or facilities) to officials or parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insider trading prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: It is illegal in many jurisdictions to trade securities based on material non-public information or tip others to trade on such information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material information includes matters a reasonable investor would consider in decisions (e.g., acquisitions/divestments, change in majority control, internal forecasts, budgets/targets, financial results, growth/expansion plans, senior management changes). Do not purchase or sell stock or pass material non-public information to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raising questions, reporting concerns and non-retaliation (Speak-Up)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees and third parties should ask questions and raise concerns; Springer Nature provides a Speak-Up system (BKMS) and prohibits retaliation against good-faith reporters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use group/business unit policies, consult management/HR/Compliance, or use BKMS (secure third-party system permitting anonymous reports in any language; no IP addresses collected). Anyone (employees, business partners, authors, suppliers, editors, customers) can use Speak-Up. No retaliation will be tolerated; retaliation itself will lead to disciplinary action. Prompt reporting helps minimise consequences; failing to report or condoning misconduct can expose individuals and the Company to civil or criminal penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of laws, policies and decision-making expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees must comply with applicable laws; where national laws are more restrictive they take precedence, but where local laws are less restrictive employees are expected to follow Springer Nature’s Code and Global Policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees should take sound business decisions informed by internal policies and seek advice when unsure. Those responsible for business across countries must be aware of cultural differences and local legal restrictions and consult in-house Legal Counsel or Group Compliance Officer as needed. Business units may apply higher standards; the Code is a statement of minimum standards and is subject to change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities of directors, officers and managers
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior staff are expected to be role models who understand risks in their areas and design/implement internal controls while encouraging teams to ask questions and raise concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directors, officers and managers should understand major legal and reputational risks, engage in implementing appropriate internal controls to avoid infringements, and support employees who ask questions or report concerns.
